name: Oblivion Remastered Script Extender (OBSE64)
summary: The Oblivion Remastered Script Extender, or OBSE64 for short, is a modder's resource that expands the modding capabilities of Oblivion Remastered.
description:
Oblivion Remastered Script Extender v0.2.2 alpha
by Ian Patterson

The Oblivion Remastered Script Extender, or OBSE64 for short, is a modder's resource that expands the modding capabilities of Oblivion Remastered. We'll see where modding for this game goes - many things can be done from the embedded engine side, and other things can be done from the Unreal side, but communication back and forth is a problem. Support for classic OBSE's functionality is complete through release 6.

[ Compatibility ]

OBSE64 will support the latest version of Oblivion Remastered available on Steam, currently 1.512.105.0. The Gamepass/MS Store/EGS version is unsupported. Do not email asking for support.

[ Installation ]

1. Copy the dll and exe files in to your Oblivion Remastered folder. This is usually C:\Program Files\Steam\SteamApps\common\Oblivion Remastered\OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64.
2. Ignore the src folder. It is there for programmers only.
3. Make sure Steam is running, then launch the game by running obse64_loader.exe.

[ FAQ ]

* Console version?
- No, not possible due to restrictions put in place by the manufacturers.

* My virus scanner complains about obse64_loader!
- It is not a virus. To extend the game, we use a technique called DLL injection to load our code. Since this technique can also be used by viruses, some badly-written virus scanners assume that any program doing it is a virus. Adding an exception to your scanner's rules may be necessary.

* Can I modify and release my own version of OBSE64 based on the included source code?
- No; the suggested method for extending OBSE64 is to write a plugin. If this does not meet your needs, please email the contact addresses listed below.

* Can I rehost OBSE64 as part of a mod pack or otherwise rehost the files?
- No. Providing a link to https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/282 is the suggested method of distribution. Exceptions may be given under applicable circumstances; contact us at the email addresses below. This means that if you see this file available for download anywhere other than https://obse.silverlock.org, https://www.github.com/ianpatt/obse64, or on Nexus by any user other than https://www.nexusmods.com/users/2166624, that service is violating copyright. I don't like having to explicitly spell this out, but my hand has been forced. Nexus collections do not rehost the file, so that's OK. (this message was originally written before collections existed)

* Where did the log files go?
- <My Documents>\My Games\Oblivion Remastered\OBSE\Logs\

* Where does the obse.ini file go?
- OBSE\obse.ini. The .ini is generally not needed. See the whatsnew for .ini options.

* How do I uninstall OBSE64?
- Delete the .dll and .exe files starting with obse64_ from your Oblivion Remastered folder.

[ Standard Disclaimer ]

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE.

name: Universal Achievement Unblocker
summary: Standalone plugin for Steam/GamePass to prevent console from blocking achievements, and unblock existing saves.
description:
[b]The original OBR achievement unblocker[/b]: prevents achievements being blocked after using console (why even bother blocking them..?), and allows earning achievements with achievement-blocked saves, by changing just 3 bytes in memory.

[heading]Setup[/heading]Extract winmm.dll next to the OblivionRemastered-WinXXX-Shipping.exe file, in one of these folders:

[b]GamePass: [/b]
[list]
[*]XboxGames\The Elder Scrolls IV- Oblivion Remastered\Content\OblivionRemastered\Binaries\WinGDK
[/list][b]Steam:[/b]
[list]
[*]steamapps\common\Oblivion Remastered\OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64
[/list][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/282]OBSE64[/url] (Steam):[/b]
[list]
[*]Requires OBSE64 setup, extract OBSE plugin into steamapps\common\Oblivion Remastered\, so the plugin appears inside OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\OBSE\Plugins\, [b]make sure to run game through obse64_loader.exe for OBSE to load[/b]
[/list]Now run the game, warning text in console will no longer appear, using console won't block achievements, and blocked saves can unlock fine again!
[line]
This mod is standalone and doesn't require any other mods to work, but an OBSE64 plugin version is also provided for those using OBSE.

Both Steam and GamePass are supported (tested by enabling godmode with TGM and exiting sewers, achievement unlocked fine)

Steam Deck/Proton may need the following launch parameter: [b]WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winmm=n,b" %command%[/b]

Plugin uses code patterns to find where to patch, so[b] hopefully will support future game updates too[/b], though if it does break please let me know!

name: Auto Upgrade Leveled Items
summary: Automatically replaces leveled unique items obtained as quest rewards with a version fitting for your level as your character progresses. No more worrying about what level you should or shouldn't complete certain quests at!
description:
One of the biggest problems that players have with now BOTH versions of Oblivion is [b][i]one-time quest reward items[/i][/b] being [color=#cc0000]permanently set[/color] at around the level you obtain them, with most items having a different version of itself for Level 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and sometimes 30. (Also sometimes just random levels)

After a 10 hour long hyperfixation where I forgot to eat or sleep and instead just taught myself the Oblivion Construction Set and papyrus scripting in order to release the 1.0 version of this mod (thankfully I already work as a Software Developer), the days of waiting tens of levels to tell Farmer Odiil that you actually saved his farm and both his sons years ago so you can get the strongest version of [i]Chillrend[/i] are now [i][b]overrrrrrrrr[/b][/i]!

[center][color=#38761d][size=5][b]HOW IT WORKS[/b][/size][/color][/center]


[size=3][b][color=#f1c232]Auto Upgrade Leveled Items[/color][/b] [/size][i][size=1](AULI)[/size][/i][size=2] will check if you have an item, such as a Level 1 Chillrend, in your inventory, find you now just leveling up to Level 5 or even nowadays being Level 20 by the time you take it out of a chest, and automatically replace it with a version of the item more befitting an adventurer of your experience (a level 5 or level 20 chillrend)! Presuming that the item's leveled list [/size][i]has[/i][size=2] a higher level version it can upgrade to.[/size]

[size=2]If you would like the upgrading and running scripts to check if you have items to be upgraded to ONLY run once when you level up there is now a [/size][i]second, alternative[/i][size=2] version of the mod located in the Main Files titled [/size][color=#f1c232][size=3][b]"Auto Upgrade Leveled Items - On Level Up"

[/b][/size][/color]If you would like to manually cast a "spell" (lesser power) to run the scripts and upgrade any lacking leveled items whenever you would like, there is now a [i]third, alternative[/i] version of the mod located in the Main Files titled [b][color=#f1c232][size=3]"Auto Upgrade Leveled Items - Manual Spell"[/size][/color][/b]

[size=2]Some items simply don't have versions at certain level milestones, so a "[/size][i]Ring of Mind Shielding[/i][size=2]" won't upgrade upon you reaching Level 5, but it will get upgraded upon reaching Level 10, 15, and finally 25 (skipping over it's missing level 20 version).[/size]

If the item has a custom enchantment on it (I believe[b] only possible with the[color=#cc0000] Deluxe Edition[/color] items[/b]) those [color=#cc0000]enchantments [i]will[/i] be [b]lost[/b] upon the item being upgraded[/color] because your current item is being swapped out with an entirely new item. If you would like to avoid that then the Manual Spell version would be best, or stashing them away anytime you go to level up.

[size=3]This covers [color=#f1c232]over 100 [/color]different leveled items and [color=#6d9eeb]TWO leveled [i]spells[/i][/color] across base Oblivion and the Shivering Isles, [color=#6aa84f]the Remaster's Deluxe Edition Items[/color], Knights of the Nine, Mehrunes' Razor, Vile Lair, and the Fighter's Stronghold DLCs![/size]


[center][size=5][b]INSTALLATION[/b][/size][/center]
[center][size=5]﻿[color=#cc0000][b]ONLY USE ONE MAIN FILE [/b][/color][/size]
[size=2](BASED ON HOW YOU'D PREFER THE MOD TO FUNCTION)[/size][/center]
If you are having any troubles with a mod manager or would prefer to just manually install the mod, you need to drag and drop the esp file to one of the two directories below depending on what platform you are playing on. You then need to write or paste the name of the file you just downloaded, such as [b]AutoUpgradeRewards.esp[/b], into the [b]Plugins.txt[/b] file within this directory to actually put the mod into your load order. (Probably at the bottom of the load order)
[center]﻿
[color=#1e84cc][size=4]Steam[/size]
[/color](ChosenHardDriveHere):\(steam or SteamLibrary depending on if this is your main drive)\steamapps\common\Oblivion Remastered\OblivionRemastered\Content\Dev\ObvData\Data

[color=#00ff00][size=4]PC Game Pass[/size]
[/color](ChosenHardDriveHere):\XboxGames\The Elder Scrolls IV- Oblivion Remastered\Content\OblivionRemastered\Content\Dev\ObvData\Data[/center]

[left][color=#f1c232][size=5][b]F.A.Q.[/b][/size][/color][/left]
Q: Is this mod [b]retroactive[/b]?
A: Yep! Install it mid playthrough with no worries at all and any item or spell listed below will be automatically and immediately upgraded to suit your level, or will be upgraded upon you leveling up should you choose to install the On Level Up version of the mod.

Q: Is this mod [b]compatible [/b]with _____?
A: This mod should be compatible with every mod that doesn't directly change either the IDs or leveled lists of the items listed below. I know that probably sounds like nonsense to most so generally you can just consider it probably incompatible with anything that also changes Leveled Items or Quest Rewards that are listed below, any mod that doesn't touch them is all good. [color=#6aa84f]Ascension yes.[/color] [color=#cc0000]Unleveled Item Rewards and Balanced Unleveled Rewards no.[/color]

Q: Does this mod effect (your favorite item name here)?
A: If it is on the list below, yes. If it is not, then it proooobably isn't a leveled item. [b][color=#cc0000]UMBRA'S SWORD IS NOT A LEVELED ITEM.[/color][/b] If you find one that isn't here and is a leveled item (other than sigil stones [i]at the moment[/i]) then come back here and rub it in my face.

Q: Can this mod properly [i][b]downgrade[/b][/i] my items from using a mod that just gave me the max level version at a lower level?
A: Not [i]yet...[/i] but once I get the base functionality of upgrading perfect and complete for everything I want it complete for, that is one of the most common requests I will be immediately looking into. Until then I will most likely post a guide in the Articles section on how to very easily and quickly use console commands to get your item back to it's proper level ❤️

Q: Will you make a version that costs something to upgrade the items or involves a more immersion-friendly process to upgrade them?
A: I will start to consider making an alternative version and file with system(s) like this after the current, main versions and vision is about as perfect as I can get it and in a spot for me to move on from :) So hopefully very soon!

Q: Does this disable achievements?
A: Nope!

name: Oblivion Remastered Performance Fix
summary: Performance improvements and bug fixes, significant reduction to the traversal stutter. Open-source. Around +30% average FPS in open world, around +50% in 1% lowest FPS improvement. Original game fidelity. Source codes: https://github.com/LTSharpe/OblivionRemasteredPerformanceFix Video demonstration: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8WkCz6cuHk
description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
Significant improvement of performance (around +30% fps in open world, around +50% fps in lowest 1% FPS) and decrease in traversal stutter via optimization of the reverse-engineered original game code. Original game fidelity (how it looks and plays) is preserved.

Includes optimizations also to the built-in Frame Generation, and provides full support for latest AMD FSR Frame Generation if AMD FSR 3.1.4 is installed

Video illustration: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8WkCz6cuHk
Open source codes and details: https://github.com/LTSharpe/OblivionRemasteredPerformanceFix

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
Pick the file that matches your setup and extract it into the game folder (in Steam: right-click Oblivion Remastered > Manage > Browse local files). Each zip already has the game's folder layout, so nothing needs renaming or moving.

Steam: download the main file "OblivionPerfFix <version>". It puts version.dll and OblivionPerfFix.ini into OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\.

Vortex or Mod Organizer 2: install the same zip as a mod (Mod manager download). In Mod Organizer 2 the files must land in the game's folder, not in Data: use its Root Builder plugin, or extract by hand.

OBSE64, or another mod that already uses version.dll (some upscaler mods do): don't overwrite that version.dll. Download "OblivionPerfFix <version> OBSE" instead. It puts OblivionPerfFix.dll and OblivionPerfFix.ini into OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\OBSE\Plugins\, where OBSE64 loads it. A few fixes can only be installed before the game's own code runs and stay off on this route (the log says which). If both versions end up installed, the fix still loads only once.

Xbox / PC Game Pass (experimental, not tested by us yet): download "OblivionPerfFix <version> GamePass". It puts the files into OblivionRemastered\Binaries\WinGDK\ in the game's folder (usually C:\XboxGames\The Elder Scrolls IV - Oblivion Remastered\). Reports welcome.

Steam Deck / Linux (reported working by players, not tested by us): as for Steam, then add WINEDLLOVERRIDES="version=n,b" %command% to the game's launch options.

Check that it works: OblivionPerfFix.log appears next to the DLL and lists each fix as it is applied.

Settings: every fix has its own switch in OblivionPerfFix.ini (1 = on, 0 = off), explained in the file itself. Everything is on by default; you don't need to change anything.

Updating: track this mod to be notified (Vortex and Mod Organizer 2 show when a new version is out). To update, extract the new zip over the old files. If you changed settings in OblivionPerfFix.ini, set them again in the new one: new fixes come with new switches.

Uninstalling: delete version.dll (OBSE route: OblivionPerfFix.dll), OblivionPerfFix.ini and the OblivionPerfFix*.log files from the folder you installed them to.

Latest AMD FSR frame generation (optional, Radeon): download amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll from AMD's FidelityFX SDK v1.1.4: github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/blob/v1.1.4/PrebuiltSignedDLL/amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll (click "Download raw file"). In OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\, rename the game's own amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll to amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll.original as a backup, then put the downloaded file there. Enable AMD FSR frame generation in the Adrenalin overlay and frame generation in the game's settings. To undo, delete the downloaded file and rename the .original back (Steam's "Verify integrity of game files" also restores it, and so does a game update: put the 3.1.4 file back afterwards).

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]The fix is one small DLL that loads with the game. For each of its fixes (about forty) it finds the specific place in the game's code, checks that it is exactly what it expects, and changes how that code works, in memory only. Each change does [b]the same work in a cheaper way[/b]. Two of them change only [i]when[/i] something happens: far-away characters you can't see are built a few frames later, and the cells behind you are unloaded a few frames later, both in the game's own order.[/color]

[table][tr][th][color=#D4D4D8]Area[/color][/th]
[th][color=#D4D4D8]What was slow or broken[/color][/th]
[th][color=#D4D4D8]What the fix does[/color][/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Rendering[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]One thread turned each frame's drawing work into DirectX 12 commands while the other cores idled; character skeletons were copied to the graphics card with an instruction that is very slow for that memory; the weather system rebuilt the sun, sky and fog every frame; cloth copied its setup every frame[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]translate on all cores (as Unreal Engine 5.5 does), copy the same bytes the fast way, rebuild only what changed, skip identical copies. [b]+22-25% fps where the CPU is the limit[/b][/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Travel: memory[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]While you travel, the game handed memory back and asked for it again seconds later, for lighting lists, texture uploads, the graphics card's object list, grass and its own small blocks: 20-100 ms each time[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]keep the memory it will need again (bounded, and handed back when Windows runs short)[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Travel: physics[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]When a new area arrived, the physics engine rebuilt its search tree and took in thousands of trees and rocks on one thread while the frame waited[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]spread rebuilds over frames, build bodies on helper threads, file new entries in batches; collisions find exactly the same things[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Travel: characters[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]A group of characters far away was created all at once (50-100 ms); crossing into a new row of cells unloaded the old ones and their characters' animation data in one frame[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]build far, unseen characters a piece per frame; take animation data apart on helper threads; unload the cells behind you one per frame[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Threads[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]A thread waiting for something could pick up a whole navigation-map tile build while the frame waited for it (up to 2.5 s seen)[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]leave those builds to free threads (the engine's own flag, and a gap in it closed)[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Doors and start-up[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]The first frame after a door or fast travel took in all the new area's physics at once; the start-up shader build held loading screens up to 5 s longer for the first minutes[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]do the physics part behind the loading screen without simulating anything; build shaders at full pace while you are not playing[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Menus[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]Opening a menu filtered and copied a full-screen picture one pixel at a time; the Graphics page asked Windows for every display mode eight times over[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]the same picture computed many times faster; the mode list kept and re-checked[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Frame generation[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]AMD's frame generation work waited in line behind the game's own frames: -20-25% rendered fps with it on[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]run it on the graphics card's second queue (an AMD plugin setting the game leaves off): [b]+22-29% rendered fps with frame generation[/b][/color][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][color=#D4D4D8][b]Crashes and bugs[/b][/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]crashes in the game's name table, its trap code, Unreal's video-memory tidying (UE-217692) and AMD's frame generation library; FSR left off after an alt-tab[/color][/td]
[td][color=#D4D4D8]each guarded so the game carries on as it would have; FSR comes back by itself[/color][/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Not applicable[/color]

[size=4][b]Shout outs[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]All the reverse-engineering and coding work done by Claude (Anthropic) under my direction, then tested by me.[/color]

name: Natural Bodies of Oblivion (NBO) with Body Morph
summary: A nude female body replacer for all races with optional Body Morphing and extended skeleton (WIP).
description:
[u][b][color=#ffe599][size=4]A Morphable Female Body & Skeleton Framework for [i]Oblivion Remastered[/i][/size][/color]

[/b][/u][u][size=4][color=#ffe599]Description[/color]
[/size][/u]
[b]Natural Bodies of Oblivion (NBO) [/b]began as a simple body replacer, intending to provide a new and enhanced nude female body. It has since evolved into a flexible morphing framework that allows the user to fully customize female characters in [i]Oblivion Remastered[/i]. With NBO's Body Morpher extension, players can adjust body shapes and physics not only for the player character but for NPCs as well - all in-game, in real-time.

[b][color=#c9daf8]The Body[/color][/b]
The "Natural" in NBO refers to this new body model that was designed with more natural curves in mind. This does not overhaul the shape of the female body but instead attempts to enhance it with extra curves and fully rigged anatomical elements. The mesh is a custom one, based on the vanilla model, and has extra mesh density around the chest and crotch areas.

[b][color=#c9daf8]Custom Expanded Skeleton[/color]
[/b]A new additional skeleton that sits alongside the old humanoid one (not a replacer) that adds bones for physics, morphing and future animation frameworks. 

[b][color=#c9daf8]Body Morpher[/color]
[/b]If the shape of the default body is not to your liking, you can jump into the body morpher at any time in game using a keybind (default: ,). You can tweak the overall look of the body or go into specific detail in certain areas. You can also adjust the physics values to reduce or increase the intensity of jiggle physics. Every change you make gets saved to a JSON file, meaning these changes persist across game sessions and also get loaded for NPCs. 

[b][color=#c9daf8]Optimization[/color]
[/b]The body has been completely lodded for all its variants and the textures use vanilla texture compression settings, hopefully preserving the same level of optimization as the vanilla game. The newly added bones for the morphing system, however, may introduce a [i]slight [/i]performance hit.

[size=4][u][color=#ffe599]Requirements[/color]
[/u][/size]
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/32]UE4SS [/url]﻿- Required for the Body Morpher
[/list]
If you want to simply replace the body mesh using NBO's default shape, then you can download the [b]light [/b]version of the mod which does not include body morphing functionality.

[color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Installation[/u][/size][/color]

[list=1]
[*]Install UE4SS if you haven't already [i](Do not install the Signatures optional file)[/i]
[*]Launch the game once - without obse_loader.exe if you use [b]OBSE[/b]. 
[*]Extract the main zip file to your Oblivion Remastered root directory (where the game's .exe is located).
[*][b]IMPORTANT:[/b] Download any updates[i] [/i]and makes sure to extract and overwrite your files with the updated versions.
[*](Optional) If using the light version of the mod, step 3 and 4 are the only steps you'll need to follow.
[/list]
If you use the [b][i][color=#6aa84f]Game Pass[/color][/i] [/b]version of the game, you'll need to modify the installation slightly:

[list=1]
[*]Follow the above steps.
[*]Navigate to your Oblivion Remastered folder and then go to [color=#a4c2f4]"OblivionRemastered/Binaries".[/color]
[*]Rename [b]"Win64"[/b] to [b]"[/b][b]WinGDK"[/b].
[/list]
As I do not own the game on [b][i][color=#6aa84f]Game Pass[/color][/i][/b], I have not verified if this works. If there are more steps involved, I will update these instructions.

[b]NOTE:[/b] If you're trying to install the mod using [i]Mod Organizer 2[/i], you're going to run into issues as [i]MO2 [/i]will try and place all .pak/.utoc/.ucas files into ~mods. You'll need to manually move files with the name [i]NaturalBodyMorph [/i]to [color=#9fc5e8]"Content/Paks/LogicMods"[/color].

[color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Using Presets
[/u][/size][/color]
Presets are stored in the following folder:
[color=#a4c2f4]"Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/Mods/NaturalBodyMorph/BodyData/Presets"

[/color][i]Presets.txt[/i] is a list of available presets that appear in the game's UI. To add a new preset:

[list=1]
[*]Drop the preset .json file into the folder above.
[*]Add its filename to [i]presets.txt[/i] (one per line).
[/list]
Alternatively, you can repopulate [i]presets.txt[/i] in one of two ways:

[list=1]
[*]Use the [b]Scan For Presets[/b] button in the [i]Body Morpher UI[/i] to automatically detect and list all presets in the folder.
[*]Run the provided .bat file, which will recreate presets.txt based on all .json files in the folder.
[/list]
[color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Keybind Configuration[/u][/size][/color]

To change the Body Morpher's activation key, navigate to:
[color=#a4c2f4]"Oblivion Remastered/OblivionRemastered/Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/Mods/NaturalBodyMorph"[/color]

Open [b]config.json[/b] and look for [b]"[/b][b]Keybind - Open Body Morph UI"[/b]. Here you can set the [b]"Key"[/b] value to whatever you want and also set up a modifier key so that opening the menu requires a combination. Here's an example for "Shift+B":

[code]﻿﻿  "Keybind - Open Body Morph UI":{
    "Key":"B",
    "ModifierKeys":["SHIFT"]
  },
[/code]
Special characters such as commas, periods and plus signs require a specific name to be used. For example, a comma is "OEM_COMMA". To find a full list of valid keys, navigate to: [color=#a4c2f4]"[/color][color=#a4c2f4]Oblivion Remastered\OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\ue4ss\Mods\Keybinds\Scripts"[/color] in the "main.lua" script file.

[b][color=#e06666][size=3]Keybinds Not Working[/size][/color][/b]

If you can't get the Keybind to work double check your installation. Vortex in particular can cause files to become displaced if it doesn't follow the "OblivionRemastered" root folder structure. Double check and make sure everything is in the right location.

[color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Uninstallation[/u][/size][/color]

[list=1]
[*]Delete the folder: [color=#a4c2f4]"OblivionRemastered/Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/Mods/NaturalBodyMorph"[/color]
[*]Remove the three [b]NaturalBodyMorph [/b]files from: [color=#a4c2f4]"OblivionRemastered/Content/Paks/LogicMods"[/color]
[*]Delete the [b]NaturalBodies[/b] folder from: [color=#a4c2f4]"OblivionRemastered/Content/Paks/~mods"[/color]
[/list]
To uninstall the underwear version of the mod, simply go to the[color=#a4c2f4] "~mods/NaturalBodies"[/color] directory and delete all files named "NaturalBodies_BUnderwear_P".

[color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Compatibility[/u][/size][/color]

[size=2]These do not cover major mod conflcits that happen as a result of other script mods. Old versions of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/1623]Hide Helmets[/url], for example, can cause a crash.
[/size]
[color=#00ff00]Compatible[/color]:
[list]
[*]Vanilla overlay mods (such as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/1284]Realistic Skin[/url]﻿﻿)
[*]Face texture or head replacer mods (So long as they don't introduce seams on the vanilla mesh)
[/list]
[color=#e06666]Not Compatible[/color]:
[list]
[*]Any female body replacers that aren't NBO
[*]Vanilla-Based Male body replacers (Use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/3696]Natural Male Bodies[/url]﻿)
[*]Body retextures that replace the texture files for female character bodies
[*]Non-NBO armors. This includes vanilla armors. There are some replacers but you'll have to search for them (I'll make a proper list later).
[/list][color=#ffe599][size=4][u]Known Issues[/u][/size][/color]

[*][b]Mod is in Beta:[/b] This mod is a work in progress. Bugs, crashes and other problems may appear. Basic troubleshooting is expected (check your mod list, UE4SS install etc.)
[*][b]No time freeze in Body Morpher:[/b] Enemies can still attack so make sure to only activate it when you know you're safe. Dialogue will kick you out.
[*][b]Clipping is expected:[/b] Armor support is limited and any armors without the new bones, will look odd when morphing the body. This also currently applies to vanilla.
[*][b]Steam version only tested:[/b] Gamepass will mostly likely work, but it’s untested. The steps to install [i]might [/i]be different.
[*][b]Neck seams:[/b] For the most part, neck seams have been reduced but as I didn't want to edit face textures for this mod, some seams are unavoidable for now.
[*][b]UI lockup bug:[/b] Pressing the Body Morpher before fade-in may cause your cursor to not appear, resulting in being locked in the Body Morph menu. Use the console (¬, ' or /) to bring up the cursor and click “Accept”.
[*][b]Argonian tail seam:[/b] Untextured section may show when certain sliders are active.
[*][b]Jagged weighting:[/b] Some belly/waist areas suffer from bone influence limits. This can be fixed but is finicky and time consuming.

If you want to report a new bug, make sure to include what race you're playing and whether or not the underwear addon is installed. It's important as each race uses a different body, so if you have a problem, it will make it easier to find if that information is shared.

[u][color=#ffe599][size=4]To Do / Planned Features[/size][/color][/u]

As mentioned, this mod is in beta and so there's still plenty to do. My current priorities after this release are:

[list]
[*]Create a system to allow the reduction of jiggle on certain armors.
[*]Armor/Cloth fitting morphs for cleavage, squish and more (Will need to hear from [b]Armor Creators[/b] on what is desired).
[*]Add support for vanilla armor/clothing (Pretty big task...)
[*]Improved skin weights - this always seems to be a thing sadly.
[*]Modder documentation to either edit/improve the body or adding a new entire body to the Body Morpher system.
[/list]
[size=4][u][color=#ffe599]FAQ[/color]
[/u][/size]
[b][color=#e06666]Q: What versions of the mod are available?[/color][/b]
There are two different main files:
[list]
[*][b]NaturalBodies-Full:[/b] This is the full mod, Body Morpher included. Requires UE4SS.
[*][b]NaturalBodies-Light: [/b]This is the body replacer without any of the Body Morphing functionalty or the custom skeleton (use this if experiencing crashes).
[*][b](Optional) NaturalBodies-Underwear: [/b]This adds the vanilla underwear back onto the body meshes. (not compatible with the light version)
[/list]
[b][color=#e06666]Q: Will you make a male version?[/color][/b]
[s]Not at the moment. I plan on releasing resources to help support anyone who wants to build a male equivalent of NBO for use with Body Morpher. However, if a significant amount of time passes without anyone making one, I may step in to do it for parity's sake. 
[/s]Yes: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/3696]https://www.nexusmods.com/oblivionremastered/mods/3696[/url]

[b][color=#e06666]Q: This mod isn't compatible with an armor I use![/color][/b]
Indeed, that's expected. Most existing armor mods won't work out of the box with NBO's skeleton and Morphs. It will either be up to the original mod creator or someone else to make it compatible. The steps actually quite simple:
[list]
[*]Reshape the mesh to fit the body.
[*]Weight the shaping bones to the cuirass (greaves and so on should use the vanilla bones).
[/list]
[b][color=#e06666]Q: Will Body Morpher work with other body mods?[/color][/b]
No, not without extra setup. However, I plan to eventually release documentation and tools for others to implement their own morphing-compatible bodies using the Body Morpher system.

[b][color=#e06666]Q: Can I use this without UE4SS?[/color][/b]
Yes - use the [b]Light[/b] version. The Body Morpher requires UE4SS for Lua scripting.

[b][color=#e06666]Q: There’s too much/little jiggle. Can I change that?[/color][/b]
Yes - jiggle strength can be adjusted directly in the [b]Body Morpher[/b] UI.

[b][color=#e06666]Q: Why make a light version?[/color][/b]
Because this mod was originally just a body replacer. I was tempted to release this mod separately to the Body Morpher but realized that it would probably lead to confusion and people attempting to use the Body Morpher with unsupported bodies.

[b][color=#e06666]Q: The Body Morpher UI won't open![/color][/b]
You've definitely messed up somewhere with your installation. Make sure you're not manually placing files where they don't belong (Like putting Logic Mods in ~mods) and make sure that your UE4SS installation is set up correctly.

[b][color=#e06666]Q: Sliders won't show up![/color][/b]
You need to be playing a female character for sliders to show up, even if you only plan to use this for NPCs.

[b]Additional Note:[/b]
I’m putting together a fairly large [i]modder’s resource pack[/i] for all of NBO, which will make it easier for others to add features or make edits. Once it’s ready, you’ll find it on this page.

name: Unleveled Item Rewards
summary: Makes all leveled items in the game unleveled, because this very concept infuriates me. Like my god, why? WHY? What kind of insanity made anyone think this was a good idea?
description:
Despite Todd's unbreakable promise that the levelling system in Oblivion had been "fixed" this is, sadly, not the case. When I learned that quest rewards STILL pull from a levelled pool I was overcome with an impossible incomprehensible fury. I blacked out, but when I awoke this mod suddenly existed.

This mod makes it so that any levelled quest reward in all the base game and all the DLC (I may have missed some so tell me if I did) will always be the best possible quest reward you could get. This is because anything is heinous and unacceptable. 


[b]FEATURES:[/b]
-All quest reward items are unlevelled. 
-All rewarded items from quests are unlevelled.
-This includes things in Knights of the Nine, Mehrunes Razor, and Shivering Isles (including the armor that you get from the various deranged craftsmen in New Sheoth).
-Yes, it's retroactive: That means that the weapons and knickknacks you have will be levelled to their appropriate versions.

[b]INSTALLATION:[/b]
-Take the ESP included in this and add it to OblivionRemastered/Content/Dev/ObvData/Data. Then add the esp included in this mod to your plugins.txt file for Oblivion. If you have the deluxe edition, take that esp and do the same thing so that your plugins.txt file has both esps inside it. 

[b]THANKS:[/b]
-To the Tamriel Rebuilt discord for saving me some time by pointing out that someone had to come in and fix this stupidity.
